messages:
Alex (IC): hi team — planning a 12-week unpaid sabbatical starting July. can i keep contributing to my 401(k) and HSA while i'm out? i'd like to keep employer contributions coming if possible.

Dana (People Ops): short version: payroll can't deduct from pay that doesn't exist, so ongoing payroll pre-tax contributions stop during unpaid leave. there are a few options though depending on what you want to keep active.

Tom (Payroll): exactly. options we support: 1) accelerate your deferral before leave so more is taken in the last paid checks, 2) set up a vendor-initiated ACH/contribution to the retirement plan if the plan allows outside contributions, or 3) make post-payroll personal contributions after you return. payroll cannot create a retro paycheck to collect missed deferrals. next payroll-election cutoff for changes is 2026-06-15 for a 7/1 effective date.

Lina (Benefits Custodian): adding vendor-side detail: our plan allows one-off employee-originated transfers into the 401(k) account using the "employee contribution remittance" form, and we can accept recurring ACH contributions from the employee's bank in some cases (requires a signed ACH authorization and plan admin approval). recurring ACHs are subject to trustee rules and may take 4-6 weeks to activate. ACH/contact link: https://benefits-custodian.example/forms/ach-auth

Alex (IC): if i do an ACH from my bank, does employer match still apply?

Lina (Benefits Custodian): employer match is only applied to amounts that hit via payroll deferrals unless your employer explicitly credits non-payroll employee contributions. the standard is: no payroll deferral = no automatic match. Dana/People Ops would need to approve any discretionary employer contribution for leave.

Dana (People Ops): we can consider a discretionary leave contribution for limited cases but it's not standard policy. please submit a leave request with compensation details and we can route to leadership for a decision.

Tom (Payroll): HSA specifics: payroll pretax HSA deductions stop on unpaid leave. however, you can make post-tax contributions directly to the HSA custodian and then claim the tax deduction on your individual return (consult a tax advisor). some custodians also accept ACH recurring deposits. employer HSA contributions (if any) follow company policy and usually stop if there are no payroll deductions unless otherwise agreed.

Alex (IC): what about health coverage while i'm on unpaid leave? COBRA?

Dana (People Ops): for leaves that are unpaid and exceed our paid leave period, COBRA or continuation options apply. we'll send the benefits continuation packet when your leave is approved. coverage and subsidy rules vary by leave type (FMLA vs unpaid sabbatical).

Tom (Payroll): example fields for the ACH setup (if you go that route):
```
Full name: Alex Rivera
Employee ID: 98765
Type of contribution: Employee after-tax (one-time) OR Recurring ACH
Bank acct last4: 4321
Desired start date: 2026-07-15
Amount: $2,500 (one-time) or $500/mo (recurring)
```

Lina (Benefits Custodian): note on contribution limits: any ACH or trustee deposit still counts toward annual IRS limits (pre-tax + Roth + after-tax where applicable). if you are 50+, catch-up rules apply. we'll validate amounts on submission.

Dana (People Ops): no manager approval needed to change deferrals while you're on payroll, but manager sign-off isn't required for ACH contributions either. manager only needs to approve leave itself per normal process.

HR Bot: benefits packet emailed to Alex (file id: bp_202606). :email:

Alex (IC): helpful, thanks. one last: will my vesting be affected by unpaid days?

Lina (Benefits Custodian): vesting continues to be based on service/tenure. unpaid leave may or may not count as service depending on plan rules; our plan treats approved unpaid leave as counted service for vesting purposes (confirm via the signed leave approval).

Dana (People Ops): i'll DM you the ACH form, the leave packet, and the payroll cutoff calendar. tagging this resolved for now — follow up if you want us to route a discretionary contribution request. :white_check_mark:
